Author: Suvra Ghosh
Bench: Suvra Ghosh
13.09.2024 rc/ct.no.34 Item No.01 Wpa No. 1942 of 2023 With Can No. 1 of 2023 Abusalam Sekh
Versus State of West Bengal & Ors.

Mr. Prosenjit Mukherjee Ms. Manisa Mandal ...for the petitioner Mr. Subrata Bhattacharjee Ms.
Shipra Santra ...for the NHAI Mr. Santanu Kumar Mitra Mr. Amartya Pal ...for the State Heard learned counsels for the parties.

The petitioner seeks extension of interim order granted by this Court vide order passed on February 09, 2023 on the ground that a further notice has been issued on August 29, 2024 by the National Highway Authority of India ('NHAI', in short) to the petitioner requesting the latter to vacate the plot in question within 15 days of receipt of the notice.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in the event the structure standing thereon is demolished by the authority in course of construction of highway, compensation payable to the petitioner cannot be assessed.
Learned counsels for the opposite parties submit that the interim order granted earlier has already expired on June 30, 2023 and was not extended further.
The land in question is vested land and the petitioner is not entitled to any compensation for the same.

It appears that the earlier notice issued by the NHAI on January 13, 2023 was stayed till March 31,
2023 vide order passed on February 09, 2023 which was subsequently extended till June 30, 2023.
The interim order was not extended thereafter and expired due to efflux of time.

Vide order dated April 03, 2024, this Curt has taken note of a notification issued under Section 4(1)
of the West Bengal Estate Acquisition Act, 1953 demonstrating that all estates and the rights of every intermediary in each such estate situated in the district of Bardhaman would vest in the State free from all encumbrances.

Plot No. 2576 was referred to as a private plot in the nature of Sali in the notification issued by the NHAI under Section 3A(1) of the National Highway Authority of India Act,
1956.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner applied for recording his name in the record of rights and his name was mutated under Section 50 of the West Bengal Land Reforms Act, 1955.

The plot being subsequently recorded in favour of the Collector under Khatian No. 1, the petitioner sought correction of the record of rights which was turned down by the prescribed authority and the revenue officer by an order passed on April 13, 2022.
Neither the vesting nor the order of the revenue officer was challenged by the petitioner.
Primary grievance of the petitioner is that it shall be difficult for him to get compensation if the present notice is implemented.

sentences.text: Since the interim order pertaining to the earlier notice does not exist at present, the question of extension of the same does not arise.
Also, the petitioner has come up before this Court assailing the subsequent notice issued on August 29, 2024.
The claim of the petitioner with regard to the plot in question shall be determined at the time of final hearing of the application.
In the event the petitioner is found to be entitled to compensation it shall be incumbent upon the authority to disburse the same in favour of the petitioner.

If the notice dated August 29, 2024 is implemented by the NHAI, the authority is directed to take measurement of the entire land and structure which they intend to take possession of in presence of the petitioner or his legal representative and the State.
With the above direction and observation the application being CAN No. 1 of 2023 is disposed of.

Let the writ petition being WPA No. 1942 of 2023 appear in the monthly list of December, 2024.
Urgent certified website copy of this order, if applied for, be supplied to the parties upon compliance with all requisite formalities.
(Suvra Ghosh,J)
